Certified records or a transcript from an elementary, secondary or postsecondary school qualify as secondary identity evidence when they show the applicant’s full name, preferably with birth date.

Mortgage or home-equity papers can establish residence when they show the applicant’s name and address, with a rural address accepted if no other physical address exists.

A payroll check or stub, bank statement, utility bill or hookup order, or canceled mail can prove residence when dated or issued within four months before application and showing the applicant’s name and residential address.
A homeless applicant must give a descriptive location address and separate mailing address, plus a social-service agency’s letterhead statement verifying homelessness and that location.

why_how.text: REAL ID applicants must provide unaltered required documents for each required step, with agency certification or MVD verification where required.
The REAL ID identity step requires proof of current legal name, birth date and United States citizenship or other lawful federal authorization to be present.
For REAL ID, proof of an issued Social Security number must show the applicant’s name and full number, which is checked with the Social Security Administration.
REAL ID residence proof requires two acceptable documents bearing the applicant’s name and current physical address; they must be unexpired or within one year of expiration.
REAL ID residency documents may be of the same type.
When the current legal name differs from the identity or Social Security documents, a REAL ID applicant must document every legal name change back to the original documented name.
